_about: Fixes to where posts were filed by the export, applied by clean_studies.py on every run (the export itself is never edited). "with": a chapter whose commentary was posted with another chapter. "copy"/"move": post ids filed under the wrong chapter, copied (the commentary covers both) or moved to the chapter they belong to. "add": commentary missing from the export, pasted from the channel, added to the chapter's study.

**Joshua 19:47**
*And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.*

**Judges 17-18** tells the story of Micah, his creation of his own church full of idols and icons, an ephod and teraphim, and his recruiting of a young Levite to be his personal house priest, calling him "father."

In those days there was no king in Israel. And men did as seemed right in their own eyes.

The story presented occurs during the period immediately after Joshua's death, where Dan had not fully gone out to take their inheritance from those that dwelled there.

**Joshua 23:4-5**
*Behold, I have divided unto you by lot these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even unto the great sea westward. And the LORD your God, he shall expel them from before you, and drive them from out of your sight; and ye shall possess their land, as the LORD your God hath promised unto you.*

Joshua had waxed old and died before the tribes had finished the work to go out and possess the land given them. Dan especially was shown to be dragging behind the other tribes.

And here they are seeking to go out and find land to take. In **Judges 18**, we find that the troop of spies stop at Mt Ephraim, and lodge at the house of Micah. There they recognized the young Levite, and inquire why he's there. He tells them of the arrangements made with Micah, his hire and role as a private priest over a house of gods.

They ask him for God's blessings in finding a suitable city to take, and he says reassuring words that God had blessed their endeavors. And so, 600 Danites set forth to go into the land, armed for war.

They come up on the house of Micah and the spies tell their army about the gods and the silver graven image and the ephod and priest, and they go in and take all the idols and ephod for themselves. The priest protests and they tell him to come with them and be their priest, and he agrees.

Micah seeing this runs out with some men from his town and Micah confronts them. The much larger force of men gathered for war tell him to stop, or he may forfeit his and his family's lives.

And so Dan finds the city of Laish, or Leshem, and the people there living simple and peaceful lives, and take it for themselves, renaming the city Dan.

And the young priest of the Levites turns out to be the son of Gershom, he and his sons, with their stolen idols and icons and fake Ephod, become the priests for the tribe of Dan until the captivity of the land. The seeds of their own downfall sown by rejecting the way of the Lord and turning to idols.

A people can seem mighty, and put many simple peasants to the sword while carrying the banner of conquest, and relying on idols and images. Unqualified priests. But in the end, God will judge them and their abominations.

Danites went marching on a crusade with their apostate priest and easily took the land, but lost their understanding. The parallel with Roman Catholics should be obvious. The end of those people being captivity and destruction, if they don't turn from Idolatry, repenting towards the Lord.

**Joshua 13** maps for us visual types.

With the majority of the warfare over. And the Lord having delivered the Israelites the land, and Joshua, who was with Moses from the beginning of the exodus, is getting old, God commands the land be apportioned, beginning east of the Jordan in the area Moses had promised Gad, Manasseh and Ruben. And of the Levites, a place in each so their priestly inheritance may be practiced in the sacrifices they maintained.

We see potential for trouble in that there are still strangers of the Canaanites among them. The seeds planted that will cause problems down the line.

As the book of **Numbers** begins to wind down, and Moses nears the end of his life, the Lord reiterates His ordinances and feasts. There is a new high priest. The men of the first generation having all died in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua.

The Lord lays out the requirements for the continual burnt sacrifices and sabbath sacrifices and the offerings made for sin.

Each has its specific requirements, varying by the day or type. The offerings of lambs or kids or bullocks. The flour and oil to be given. And the drink offerings poured out.

All a picture of Jesus. All a continuous savor to the Lord. As the children of Israel reach the promised land, they are called to remember these ordinances for all time, that their faith in the Lord not be forgotten, and His favor given them.

Verse 7 contains a description of the drink offering.

*And the drink offering thereof shall be the fourth part of an hin for the one lamb: in the holy place shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured unto the Lord for a drink offering.*

This is a verse that could be used to defend the consumption of alcohol, or the blasphemy of using fermented wine at the Lord's supper, although it rarely is.

But the prohibition against the priests consumption of strong wine;

**Leviticus 10:8-9**
*And the Lord spake unto Aaron, saying, Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations:*

...and the numerous places in scripture that teach against it present a problem for those seeking to use this verse to justify it.

But what then? First, we see the drink offering is to be poured out with the burnt offering, which is a continual fire. Alcoholic strong drink would feed the fire, where new wine would quench it. Also, where fermented juices store easily, there is the idea that in the wilderness it would be easiest to obtain and have on hand for the purpose of a twice daily sacrifice.

Ellicott's Commentary states:
(7) Shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured . . . --Better, pour out the drink offering of strong drink. The word shecar, which is here rendered "strong wine," denotes any kind of intoxicating drink, whether made from grapes, honey, or grain; but it is more frequently used to denote a drink which is not made from grapes, as, e.g., in Leviticus 10:9, where the command is given to Aaron and his sons not to drink "wine nor strong drink" (shecar) when they went into the tent of meeting. In the parallel passage in Exodus, the drink offering was to consist of "the fourth part of an hin of wine" (Numbers 29:40). (Comp. Numbers 15:5.) In Exodus 30:9 it is forbidden to pour any drink offering upon the altar of incense, from which passage it has been inferred that the drink offerings were poured upon the altar of burnt sacrifice.

The indication that strong wine is liquor from other sources than grapes, which has weak fermentation.

Matthew Henry commentary says;
The daily sacrifice is called a continual burnt-offering; when we are bid to pray always, at least every morning and evening we should offer up solemn prayers and praises to God. Nothing is added here but that the wine poured out in the drink-offering is to be strong wine, to teach us to serve God with the best we have. It was a figure of the blood of Christ, the memorial of which is still left to the church in wine; and of the blood of the martyrs, which was poured out as a drink-offering on the sacrifice and service of our faith, Php 2:17.

I only note these to show that this passage is unique in what it commands, and the reason unclear other than to suppose it is a libation for God, and His will it be offered.
